Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L07_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which speech plan is most complete?

answer.text: A. Topic only: presentations.

feedback.text: A topic alone is incomplete because it does not include focus, points, support, or transitions.

answer.text: B. Focus, three related points, support, reasoning, transitions, and conclusion.

feedback.text: Correct. This plan includes the major parts needed for an integrated informative speech.

answer.text: C. Three unrelated facts about school.

feedback.text: Unrelated facts do not create a coherent informative speech plan.

answer.text: D. A full paragraph to read aloud.

feedback.text: A full script may prevent natural speech delivery and does not show planning parts clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L07_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Point: Organized notes improve delivery. Which support best fits?

answer.text: A. Some notes use blue ink.

feedback.text: This detail does not explain how notes improve delivery.

answer.text: B. Delivery is part of speaking.

feedback.text: This repeats the topic without supporting the point.

answer.text: C. Notes grouped by main point help the speaker find the next idea quickly.

feedback.text: Correct. This support explains how organized notes improve delivery.

answer.text: D. Some speeches are short.

feedback.text: This does not support the point about organized notes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L07_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: Practicing aloud helps speakers notice unclear sections before presenting. Which paraphrase is accurate?

answer.text: A. Rehearsing out loud can help speakers find confusing parts before the presentation.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning and changes the wording.

answer.text: B. Practicing aloud makes every speech perfect.

feedback.text: This exaggerates the source and changes the meaning.

answer.text: C. Speakers should never revise unclear sections.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source meaning.

answer.text: D. Presenting is the same as reading silently.

feedback.text: This adds an inaccurate idea that is not in the source.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L07_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which note is most speech-ready?

answer.text: A. Say everything about speeches.

feedback.text: This is too vague to guide delivery.

answer.text: B. Read the full source paragraph.

feedback.text: This may lead to reading instead of presenting.

answer.text: C. Random speaking ideas.

feedback.text: This does not follow a useful format.

answer.text: D. Point 1: outline order; support: steps help audience follow.

feedback.text: Correct. This note gives a clear point and support cue.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L07_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which transition best connects organization to support?

answer.text: A. Next thing.

feedback.text: This does not show how the ideas connect.

answer.text: B. After organizing the main points, the speaker needs support that explains each point.

feedback.text: Correct. This transition shows a clear relationship between planning and support.

answer.text: C. I am changing to something else.

feedback.text: This signals a shift but does not connect ideas.

answer.text: D. Anyway, support.

feedback.text: This is too casual and unclear for informative speaking.
